speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We will always have some people who are not happy but 91% said this.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Over the years, through the consistent upholding and exemplification of these values, the Police have built an enormous reservoir of trust and confidence with the public.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: That is a huge benefit, not just to the Police but also to Singaporeans as a whole.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Whenever any allegation is received, the first task of the Police is to investigate the allegation quite carefully and thoroughly.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: For example, The Online Citizen (TOC) glorifies in running the Police down with a series of untrue stories.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I referred to some stories last year on their untruths.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: It was designed to make people angry: falsehood.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The man was never accused of being involved in any motor vehicle theft, nor was he asked to provide any statement at a Police station.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: It is not to say that the Police do not make mistakes.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: It is not to say that some policemen do not commit offences.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Therefore, there can be no objection to comments, feedback, fair criticism, complaints.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And all of them will be looked at.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: You read of Police Officers, other public servants, being charged in Court where criminal action is warranted and they face the consequences.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: That is why people have faith in the system.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, we have to take the question of fake news about Police and other agencies seriously and deal with it.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I notice that over the past few months when people made false and malicious allegations against the Police, the Police issue a correction.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Unless the Government takes action to protect the integrity of Government institutions, I am concerned that the trust and faith in Government institutions will be undermined.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: But I am referring to false and malicious allegations against the Police.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I will distinguish between three types of situations.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It could be in error where the person could have made a mistake, but genuine, well-intentioned feedback or complaints because there is a difference of viewpoints, allegations based on an honest belief in certain facts.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Generally, there should be no consequences for that.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The second category where the complaint is justified, feedback is justified, and we must take action.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The third category is what the Member is focused on, which is, false, deliberate, malicious allegations.
